Placemaker.Waterfront.Name: Waterfront
Placemaker.Recipe.Waterfront.Description: A designed edge to the water, fitted to the terrain: a quay, walkway quay, boardwalk or natural bank at the water, a smooth embankment up to one level promenade with benches facing the water, lamps, planted beds and trees, piers from landings, step flights down to the river. Cliffs stay natural, with a cliff-top walk.
Placemaker.Waterfront.style.Tooltip: Promenade boardwalk, pier park, harbour quay, river steps or natural bank: each sets the water edge, the promenade and the planting.
Placemaker.Waterfront.waterSide.Tooltip: Which side of the area faces the water. Automatic finds the water; otherwise pick a side (north = +Z on the map).
Placemaker.Waterfront.promWidth.Tooltip: Distance from the water to the promenade (on a harbour quay: the depth of the paved apron behind the quay).
Placemaker.Waterfront.railings.Tooltip: One continuous railing along the promenade's water edge, only where the ground there drops more than 1 m (quays and piers bring their own).
Placemaker.Waterfront.lampSpacing.Toolti: Lamps along the water side of the walk. 0 = none.
Placemaker.Waterfront.moorings.Tooltip: Bollards along the quay edge, as in a harbor.
Placemaker.Waterfront.riprap.Tooltip: Rocks along the waterline (riprap), for a natural bank.
Placemaker.Waterfront.steps.Tooltip: Paved flights on the smooth bank from the promenade down to the walkway quay: a few spots, or regularly along the whole edge.
Placemaker.Waterfront.stepLevels.Tooltip: Unused since s30: the flights lie on the smooth bank (no terraces).
Placemaker.Waterfront.piers.Tooltip: Piers built as paths out over the water. They reach past the outline over the water when the area is drawn along the shore.
Placemaker.Waterfront.pierHeads.Tooltip: A cross walk at the end of each pier.
Placemaker.Waterfront.fishing.Tooltip: Spots along the edge with fishing props, a seat and a bin.
Placemaker.Waterfront.nautical.Tooltip: Life rings by the edge, anchors, buoys and crates along the walk.
Placemaker.Waterfront.trees.Tooltip: A tree row, or a double row (avenue), behind the promenade.
Placemaker.Waterfront.backdrop.Tooltip: What fills the land behind the promenade: a lawn, a planted park, or nothing.
Placemaker.Waterfront.shoreTexture.Toolt: Paint a soft sand or dirt band into the terrain at the water’s edge (permanent). Automatic: sand for promenades and piers, dirt for fishing banks, none for quays.
Placemaker.Waterfront.Issue.PiersNeedWat: Piers need water beside or inside the area: draw it along the shore or out over the water.
Placemaker.Waterfront.edge.Tooltip: What meets the water: a wide quay (stone wall, deck above the water), a walkway quay, a timber boardwalk just off the bank, or a natural bank graded into the water. Automatic picks by type.
Placemaker.Waterfront.deckHeight.Tooltip: Height of the quay or boardwalk deck above the water. The land behind a quay is filled to this level (permanent).
Placemaker.Waterfront.beds.Tooltip: Beds of low flowering shrubs in the bays behind the promenade.
Placemaker.Waterfront.hillside.Tooltip: Where the level promenade is cut into rising ground: a retaining wall along its land edge (as when a road is built into a slope), a graded grass bank back up to the ground, or automatic (a wall when the cut is between 1.5 m and the wall height limit, else a bank).
Placemaker.Waterfront.maxWall.Tooltip: Highest retaining wall allowed along the promenade's land side; a taller cut gets a graded bank instead.
Placemaker.Waterfront.bay.Tooltip: Carves a bay into the land below the water level: the water flows in and the promenade follows the curved shore. 0 keeps the shore as drawn.
Placemaker.Waterfront.Issue.WallTooHigh: The hillside behind the promenade rises {0} m, above the {1} m wall limit: graded as a bank instead.
